subject: general
question: The Constitution of India does NOT consider _______ as a part of the Union Executive.

options.text: Prime Minister of India and her/his Council of Ministers

solution:
The correct answer is **"__Advocate-General of state__".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Union Executive grants the government the authority to enact laws covered by **Articles 52 to 78 of Chapter I of Part IV.**
 
• The Union Executive became the **most significant branch of government** as a result of its substantial actions.
 
• **The President, who serves as the head of state, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, who oversees the Union, and the Attorney General make up India's union executive.**
 
• The Indian Constitution **grants the President executive authority, **but he or she cannot **act alone in using it.**
 
• In order for the President to exercise executive authority,** the Prime Minister oversees the Council of Ministers.**
 
• Three people **make up India's union executive, which develops legislation and oversees parliamentary operations.**
 
• **Some important points on Advocate-General of state are:-**
 
 
• **​**The Additional Solicitor General is placed before the Advocate General of State in the Order of Precedence.
 
• Only Indian citizens are granted the right to be eligible for the position of Advocate General of State; foreigners are not permitted to hold this public office.
 
• He has the absolute right to show up in any state court.
 
• He is not permitted to cast a ballot in any state legislative committees or in any sessions of the state legislature's houses. However, he is entitled to speak and take part in these procedures.
